accepted_review_findings:
[reviewer finding R2-F1, medium] The previous finding F1 and maintainer note 0 required deleting 'image view' unless the controller grants it, and using its exact name if it is granted. The repair kept the tool and only shortened its wording. Nothing in request.json, material_reviewer.txt, the quality contract or the other controller files available to me grants an image-viewing tool to WRITE_EVIDENCE solvers. The platform check names only 'artifact read/write' and 'CPU Python execution' (paths relative to /work) for non-LIT tasks. If the tool is not granted, the solver is promised a tool that does not exist, and the judge criterion 'Readability and design quality' may implicitly assume visual self-inspection. I cannot verify the grant, so the item stays retained.
Required repair: Controller/constructor: confirm the exact WRITE_EVIDENCE tool grant. If no image-viewing tool is granted, remove 'image view' from input_contract.tools and from task.md 'Tools available to you'. Optionally say the solver may inspect its own PNG programmatically with Pillow/numpy under /work. If one is granted, cite the grant and use its exact registered name in both places. Keep the two lists identical and update the sha256 values.

[reviewer finding R2-F2, low] The sentence says every timed query terminates with a witness or a proof. The same table has PB Max = TO for Higgs/IJCNN and direct-SMT TO for R06-R13, so some queries ended at the 3600 s timeout without either outcome. The TO semantics are stated correctly elsewhere (task.md Fixed requirements; provenance timeout_marker and N5), so this is a local imprecision, not a data error. It could still lead a solver to caption all queries as decided.
Required repair: In both task.md and provenance.json, reword to: 'A query that completes ends either with a witness pair or with a proof that no such pair exists; a query that reaches the 3600 s per-query timeout is recorded as TO.' Keep the wording identical in both files and update the hashes.
controller_notes:
CONTROLLER PLATFORM STATEMENT (authoritative; the reviewer's earlier platform checklist was incomplete and omitted parts of it, which caused the tool finding below to be raised). The controller grants exactly these tools; task texts that name them as stated here are sourced and correct:
Tools the controller grants to every solver (use these exact names when a task text names a tool):
- artifact_read_write: read and write files by path RELATIVE to the working directory /work
  (write "results/x.json", never "/work/results/x.json" as a tool path).
- cpu_python_execution: run a Python script located under /work (relative path). A script shipped under the
  read-only public input root cannot be run directly; if the task wants the solver to use a supplied checker, say that
  the solver must first write a copy of it into /work (e.g. tools/check.py) and run the copy.
- artifact_image_view: view an image file the solver produced under /work (e.g. to inspect its own rendered PNG).
  Granted to every task type; a task may rely on it (e.g. WRITE_EVIDENCE figure checks) or ignore it.
LIT tasks additionally get the literature tools: literature.search(query, limit) -> document_id values of the form
  doc-<arXiv id>v<version>, title, version date, snippet; literature.read(document_id) -> record and abstract;
  literature.read_page(document_id, page_number) -> one-based controller pages of the pinned arXiv HTML text (not PDF
  pages); page text carries bracketed anchor markers that begin with the section sign. A citation locator must be a
  marker copied exactly from a page the solver read, or "abstract"; never print a concrete example anchor.
No other tools exist (no shell, no network, no model client for the solver to call directly).

Repair: keep the image-viewing tool, named artifact_image_view, in input_contract.tools and task.md; it is granted. Resolve the remaining accepted findings (timeouts in the public query-outcome statement; the visual-transcription unknown) as the reviewer requires.
